subject: Multiplexing admission policy and network playbook for private GPU pools
messages:
From: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Cc: 
Date: Thu, 15 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Draft: multiplexing admission policy + network playbook for private GPU pools

Team — attaching a compact playbook draft for the Aurelia Health private deployment. High-level goals:
- Guarantee 99th percentile latency targets for interactive routes (<= 350ms) while allowing background batch/rerank jobs to absorb tail traffic.
- Define admission thresholds and slabing strategy for multiplexed tenants so we can sustain 3x burst windows without throttling critical ops.
- Clarify network QoS and peering guidelines (egress caps, BGP prep) so their on-prem edge doesn't swamp the private pool.

What’s attached: multiplex_admission_matrix_v1.xlsx (proposal for slab sizes, per-tenant headroom, admission thresholds), vpc-network-sketch.png, mutual_action_plan_AUR-2026-0419.md (timeline + SLO commitments).

Key asks: please review the admission matrix and call out any operational risks, especially around KV cache warm-up assumptions and cross-tenant memory pressure. Also decide whether we want to provision a 10% dedicated "priority lane" for heartbeat/health-checks + urgent low-latency paths.

Timeline: I want internal alignment by EOD Monday (7/19) so we can share a finalized Mx plan with Aurelia on Tuesday.

Thanks — Neha
Neha Kapoor
Product Manager, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>, Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 16 Jul 2026 11:06:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Draft: multiplexing admission policy + network playbook for private GPU pools

Neha — I skimmed the matrix. Quick notes inline: 

- Admission thresholds: the proposal uses a tokens/sec metric per tenant. For on-prem with variable request sizes I prefer a combined metric (tokens/sec weighted by active KV entries) so an LLM-heavy low-token request doesn't get starved when a tenant has massive KV cache churn.

- Slab sizing: the suggested 8/16/32 slab tiers are fine but we should add a 4-GPU cold slab for staging and warmup to avoid noisy neighbor effects on the main pool. That can live in the same allocation domain but be marked transient.

- Autoscale triggers: need a hysteresis window. If we spin up new occupancy slabs on a transient spike <10 minutes we will oscillate. Suggest: 3-minute sampling + 20% sustained over baseline for 5 mins to trigger warm-pool ramp.

- KV cache warm-up: emphasize proactive prefix caching during warm-pool ramp. If we have customer-provided traffic traces, pre-seed the cache. Otherwise expect a 90–120s warmup hit per model variant.

I'll add a small diff to the spreadsheet and push a version.

—Karthik

From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 17 Jul 2026 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Draft: multiplexing admission policy + network playbook for private GPU pools

Thanks — good draft. Ops concerns: 

1) Network egress shaping: Aurelia's edge teams tend to misconfigure NAT pools. We should mandate a 5-tuple flow limit per staging CIDR and provide a validation script (I'll attach a small iperf/BGP sanity check in the Drive folder). If they oversubscribe egress we must have clear per-customer throttles in the admission layer.

2) Failover paths: the plan assumes fallback to a quantized variant when capacity is constrained. Ensure the automated rollback does a golden-check against a failover prompt-set (not just latency). We had one incident where accuracy regressed unnoticed.

3) Observability: add tokenized metrics: admission_denied.{tenant,reason}, slab_fill_pct, kv_cache_warmup_time, model_variant_failover_count. Hook those to alerting thresholds (P99>50ms for failover_count > 3 in 10m).

Operational ask: Diego — can you estimate the network egress budget in Mbps per tenant for the 3x burst window? I put a placeholder in the spreadsheet but need a concrete number to finalize the mutual action plan.

-jw

From: Patrick O'Neill <patrick@aurelia.ai>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
Cc: Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 18 Jul 2026 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Multiplexing admission policy and network playbook for private GPU pools

Neha — thanks for sharing. Quick questions from Aurelia infra: 

- What throughput should we guarantee per tenant in the initial commit? Their product needs steady 250 rps for low-latency chat routes and periodic batch embeds (peak 5k rps for 3–5 minute windows).
- What does the priority lane buy us in terms of lower latency (numbers)?
- Are there any configuration items Aurelia must expose from on-prem (BGP community tags, link MTU, NAT egress pool sizes) for Redwood to enforce the QoS rules?

If you can provide these as a short checklist we'll loop in Aurelia networking and schedule a verification call.

—Patrick
Aurelia Health — Infrastructure

From: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
To: Patrick O'Neill <patrick@aurelia.ai>, Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 19 Jul 2026 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Multiplexing admission policy and network playbook for private GPU pools

Patrick — answers below; I’ve attached the updated matrix (v1.1) and a one-page checklist in the Drive link. Short answers: 

- Initial per-tenant commit (baseline): guarantee sustained 250 rps for interactive chat (95th pct latency target <= 250ms). For bursts: admission policy allows up to 3x sustained baseline for 3-minute windows; we size for 5k rps peak but treat anything above 1.5k rps as burst (hot-path throttles to background class).

- Priority lane: reserved 10% of pool GPUs as a logical priority lane; in practice that reduces P95 latency by ~30–40ms under mixed load in our simulations (attached numbers). It also gives us a guaranteed path for health-checks and emergency calls; we recommend keeping it locked for control-plane / urgent low-latency routes.

- Required Aurelia config items: BGP community tagging (simple tag for tenant traffic), link MTU >= 9000 recommended for model sharding traffic, NAT pool sizing (suggest min 1k ephemeral ports per active worker IP), and a routable management VLAN for telemetry. The one-page checklist has exact commands and validation steps.

Operational next steps: 
1) Diego to confirm egress Mb/s numbers (see Jonas's ask).
2) We will schedule a 60-minute verification call Wed 7/21 to run the BGP/NAT sanity checks and run a short warmup.

I pushed the updated documents to https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1Xq-multiplex-adm-2026 (look for multiplex_admission_matrix_v1.1.xlsx).

Thanks,
Neha
